correctness.rationale: Direct 3x3 Gaussian design matrix yields det(I)=nu^{-6}(a-b)^2(a+b-2c)^2. The strict inequality log(cosh u)<u^2/2 establishes the no-null region d<=1. Strict decrease of tanh(u)/u establishes exactly one nonzero null design when d>1, and the analytic expansion gives square-root onset. Both nonzero sign lobes attain positive local maxima. Continuity of their maxima, the positive outer limit at d down to 1 and the vanishing outer-bound as d goes to infinity prove existence of at least one two-global-optimum tie. The checker independently matched the matrix determinant on representative parameters and passed 323 finite diagnostics; it is explicitly not substituted for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Three equal-cost samples provide exactly the number of observations needed to estimate two overlapping source fluxes and an unknown sky level. The theorem identifies an unexpected singular sample radius despite distinct positions, a sharp source-separation threshold, and an unavoidable tie between inner and outer globally optimal symmetric readout layouts. These nontrivial identifiability/optimization features are instrument-design cautions and exact benchmarks, not generic positivity checks or arbitrary parameter slices. Model and historical-priority limitations are prominently stated.
